title: Greetings and goodbyes
subtitle: Saludos y despedidas
review: Written by Claude in Latin American (Mexican) Spanish. Check the Spanish, the English and the notes before recording audio. English support only.

categories.desc: Hello at any hour, and the three greetings that follow the clock.
cards: For everyone, at any time of day. With a stranger, add buenos días to be polite.
Until about noon. People say it as they walk into a shop or a waiting room.
Good morning, ma'am. Do you have sweet bread?
Buenas tardes. Una mesa para dos, por favor.
Good afternoon. A table for two, please.
A hello after dark, and also a goodbye at bedtime.
Only in Mexico, and only to answer the phone.

categories.desc: Asking how someone is, and the usual answers.
cards: With tú: friends, family, people your own age.
With usted: an older person, a customer, someone you have just met.
Buenos días, don Luis. ¿Cómo está usted?
Good morning, Don Luis. How are you?
Friendly, and it works with tú and with usted. Often no real answer is expected.
Very Mexican, between friends. Not for your boss.
The standard reply. With usted: ¿y usted?
— How are you? — Fine, thanks. And you?
— ¿Qué tal? — Más o menos. Tengo mucho trabajo.
— How's it going? — So-so. I have a lot of work.

categories.desc: From the plain adiós to see you tomorrow.
cards: The plain goodbye. In Mexico people also say it in passing, to someone they walk by without stopping.
The everyday goodbye when you will see the person again, some day.
Casual. Add when: nos vemos mañana, nos vemos el lunes.
Also said at bedtime, instead of buenas noches.
Ya me voy a dormir. Hasta mañana.
I'm going to bed. See you tomorrow.

categories.desc: Announcing that you are leaving, and wishing someone well.
cards: Ya: now, already. It announces the goodbye; the goodbye itself can take a while.
Bueno, ya me voy. Es tarde.
Ahorita is Mexican for 'right now'. It can mean one minute or one hour.
Voy a la tienda. Ahorita vengo.
I'm going to the store. I'll be right back.
See you on Monday. Take care!
All the best. / Have a good one.
A warm goodbye to the person who is leaving. With usted: que le vaya bien.
Gracias por venir. ¡Que te vaya bien!
Thanks for coming. All the best!
Say hi to your mom for me.
Saludar a…: to say hello to… The answer: de tu parte.
— Salúdame a tu mamá. — De tu parte.
— Say hi to your mom for me. — I will.
